target.title: feat(feishu): configure card footer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu agent replies already render structured cards with a gray note footer, but operators cannot customize that footer from config. This makes the main agent card footer fixed to the generated `Agent / Model / Provider` metadata instead of allowing a deployment-specific label or operational note.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Feishu plugin `cardFooter` config field and wires it into the existing structured-card note rendering path instead of adding a new card layout. The setting is shared config, so it works at `channels.feishu.cardFooter` and can be overridden per account with `channels.feishu.accounts.<id>.cardFooter`.

When unset or blank, Feishu cards keep the current generated footer. That preserves existing behavior while giving operators a small, explicit customization hook for main agent cards and other agent reply cards.

## User Impact

Users can configure a custom footer note for Feishu/Lark agent cards. The value is used on both streaming cards and complete structured-card replies. Existing configs continue to show the current generated `Agent: ... | Model: ... | Provider: ...` footer when `cardFooter` is not set.

## Evidence

target.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw does not currently have an official installable MXC sandbox backend for Windows hosts that can run sandboxed commands through Microsoft eXecution Containers. This leaves MXC-capable Windows environments without a first-party plugin path for ProcessContainer-backed execution and filesystem bridge operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an official OpenShell-style external `mxc` sandbox plugin package (`@openclaw/mxc-sandbox`) with Windows-only readiness checks, plugin-owned MXC SDK dependency ownership, ProcessContainer payload construction, a plugin-side launcher, host-backed filesystem bridge support, sandbox policy loading, and targeted tests.

The plugin source lives under `extensions/mxc`, but it is packaged as an installable plugin (`bundledDist: false`) so the MXC SDK/native dependency is owned by the plugin package instead of an unshipped bundled `node_modules` tree. The backend uses the stable current MXC `0.7.0-alpha` schema and keeps sandbox defaults conservative: curated environments, headless UI, per-exec temp directories, absolute binary overrides, host-derived Windows roots, read-only default workspace access for `none`/`ro`, and fail-closed unsupported policy handling.

## User Impact

Users on MXC-capable Windows hosts can install the official MXC sandbox plugin, restart the Gateway, configure `sandbox.backend: "mxc"`, and run OpenClaw sandboxed commands through MXC. Non-Windows or unsupported Windows hosts remain unaffected because the plugin stays dormant when readiness probes fail.

Install command:

```bash
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/mxc-sandbox
```

target.title: fix(agents): use CJK-aware token estimation for tool results
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
`TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 2` 与 `estimateStringChars`的中文字符权重(4 chars/token)不匹配，导致CJK-rich内容被2倍高估，触发false token overflow错误，中断中文工作流。

例如：85k中文字符被估计为170k tokens，实际应为~85k，导致本不应触发的preemptive compaction提前激活。

## Evidence
### Verifiable Behavior
- **Issue Reference**: #95327
- **Test Results**:
```
[pnpm test] preemptive-compaction.test.ts
Tests 21 passed (21)
Duration 6.03s

CJK Text Test: 85,000+ Chinese chars estimated as ~85,000 tokens (ratio: ~1.0)
CJK Tool Result Test: 80k CJK chars fit within 128k budget with 20k reserve
Mixed Lang Test: ratio 0.8-1.5, healthy
JSON Payload Test: CJK-heavy JSON tool result no longer triggers false overflow
Non-serializable Test: circular non-array content completes precheck without throwing
```

### Real Behavior Proof
Below is the terminal output from running a standalone script against this PR branch. The script exercises the actual production estimation helpers (`estimateLlmBoundaryTokenPressure` and `shouldPreemptivelyCompactBeforePrompt`) with realistic CJK-heavy, mixed, and Latin-only tool-result payloads.

Command: `pnpm exec tsx .tmp-cjk-proof.ts`

```
=== PR #95447 real-behavior proof: CJK-aware tool-result token estimation ===

--- 85k CJK-heavy tool result ---
  Input chars:              85,000
  CJK ratio:                90.0%
  Adjusted char weight:     314,500 (CJK-aware)
  Before-fix token estimate: 165,173  (/2 ratio)
  After-fix token estimate:  94,421  (CJK-aware)
  After-fix route:          fits
  After-fix overflow:       0 tokens

--- Mixed CJK + Latin tool result (CJK majority) ---
  Input chars:              49,000
  CJK ratio:                61.2%
  Adjusted char weight:     139,000 (CJK-aware)
  Before-fix token estimate: 73,035  (/2 ratio)
  After-fix token estimate:  41,771  (CJK-aware)
  After-fix route:          fits
  After-fix overflow:       0 tokens

--- Latin-only tool result ---
  Input chars:              67,000
  CJK ratio:                0.0%
  Adjusted char weight:     67,000 (CJK-aware)
  Before-fix token estimate: 35,235  (/2 ratio)
  After-fix token estimate:  40,271  (CJK-aware)
  After-fix route:          compact_then_truncate
  After-fix overflow:       13,271 tokens

=== Result ===
CJK-heavy tool results no longer trigger false overflow;
non-CJK tool results keep the existing conservative estimate.
```

The proof shows that a 85k-character CJK-heavy tool result was previously estimated at ~165k tokens (false overflow → would route to `compact_only`) and is now estimated at ~94k tokens (fits within a 128k budget with 20k reserve → routes to `fits`). The Latin-only case still uses the conservative `/2` ratio and correctly routes to compaction when it genuinely overflows.

### Technical Evidence
- **Before**: `TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 2` 导致CJK被double-count
- **After**:
  - CJK比例≥50%时使用`ESTIMATED_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4`，与正常文本估计一致
  - 非CJK场景保持保守`/2`比例
  - JSON tool-result payload 和 unknown record fallback 现在也被纳入 CJK ratio 采样
  - ratio pre-pass 使用与 token-pressure 估算相同的 `safeJsonStringify` fallback，避免非序列化内容抛出
- **Files Changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/preemptive-compaction.ts`
  - `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts`
- **Test Updates**: `preemptive-compaction.test.ts` 增加 5 个 CJK/JSON/fallback 相关测试用例

### Regression Risk
- Low: 仅修改 tool-result token 估算路径，非 CJK 场景保持原有保守行为
- 所有 21 个估计测试通过
- 新增非序列化内容回归测试，确保 precheck 不会因 `JSON.stringify` 失败而中断 turn

## Why This Change Was Made
使 tool result token estimation 与 CJK 字符权重对齐，防止 false overflow，确保多语言工作流公平对待 CJK 字符；同时覆盖 JSON/unknown payload 和安全 fallback，避免 estimator 分支遗漏。

## User Impact
- 中文工作流不再因错误的 token overflow 中断
- Tool result 上下文预算更准确（含结构化 JSON 返回）
- 无配置或操作变更，零用户学习成本

target.title: fix #91171: [Bug]: Sub-agent model routing ignores model parameter, silently falls back to deepseek
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `sessions_spawn` could report an explicit requested model as applied while the child `agent` gateway launch still omitted provider/model and ran through the default route.
- Solution: forward the resolved provider/model into the child launch only for explicit `sessions_spawn.model`, and authorize that override at the existing gateway boundary.
- What changed: `spawnSubagentDirect` now adds provider/model to the initial child `agent` request for explicit model overrides; in-process gateway dispatch can merge internal `allowModelOverride` into the scoped client so plugin/run metadata is preserved.
- What did NOT change: no new config/schema/protocol fields; no model catalog/default policy change; no-explicit-model sub-agent spawns do not forward provider/model as explicit gateway overrides.
- Why it matters / User impact: users spawning a sub-agent for a model-specific task, such as image-capable Qwen from a default DeepSeek session, need the actual child run to use that requested model instead of silently falling back to a model without the needed capabilities.
- Fixes #91171

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Explicit `sessions_spawn.model` was resolved and reported but not passed to the child gateway `agent` request that starts the actual sub-agent run.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Windows Git Bash, using Node 22.19.0 from npm `node@22.19.0`, an isolated loopback OpenClaw gateway, and a configured Claude CLI backend for `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`; focused Vitest used the repository `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Live proof: started a local loopback gateway with isolated config/state and invoked `spawnSubagentDirect({ model: "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6", mode: "run", cleanup: "keep" })` against that gateway; then read gateway `status` for the spawned child session. Regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts`; `git diff --check`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The live spawn returned `status: "accepted"`, `resolvedProvider: "claude-cli"`, `resolvedModel: "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6"`, and `modelApplied: true` for child session `agent:dev:subagent:086240a8-3915-42ab-97e4-41b84c29704e`; a follow-up gateway `status` row for that child showed `kind: "spawn-child"`, `configuredModel: "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6"`, `selectedModel: "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6"`, and `runtime: "Claude CLI"`. The focused Vitest command exited 0, and `git diff --check` exited 0.
- **Observed result after fix:** A real local spawned child run selected the same explicit provider/model that `sessions_spawn`/`spawnSubagentDirect` resolved, instead of falling back to the default route. Tests additionally assert that explicit `sessions_spawn.model: "openai/gpt-5.4"` produces child `agent` params with `provider: "openai"` and `model: "gpt-5.4"`; in-process explicit `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` dispatch forwards provider/model with internal override authorization; no-explicit-model spawn asserts provider/model remain undefined.
- **What was not tested:** The reporter's exact live QQ/Qwen/DeepSeek channel setup was not run. The live proof uses a local Claude CLI provider/model available in this environment, exercising the same gateway launch boundary identified in the issue: whether the requested provider/model is selected by the spawned child run.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Addressed for the current author-action label by pushing the CI assertion repair and keeping the proof/maintainer-risk disclosures in this body for re-review.
- **RF-002:** Fixed the failing sub-agent test assertions: the no-explicit-model in-process path now expects no internal override option, and the explicit in-process model test checks the actual dispatch params/options without requiring absent fields as own `undefined` properties. Reran the focused subagent/gateway regression command successfully.
- **RF-003:** Disclosed in `Merge risk`: the WebSocket path uses admin scope only when an explicit provider/model override needs gateway authorization; in-process dispatch merges internal `allowModelOverride` into the scoped client instead of forcing a synthetic admin client. This auth-provider boundary remains called out for maintainer acceptance.
- **RF-004:** Disclosed: the reporter's exact QQ/Qwen/DeepSeek setup was not rerun. The live proof uses a local Claude CLI provider/model while exercising the same child gateway launch boundary and selected-model status evidence.
- **RF-005:** Addressed with a narrow automated test repair only; no product direction or production routing behavior was changed in the follow-up.
- **RF-006:** Fixed `src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts:362-400` dispatch option expectations as described in RF-002.
- **RF-007:** Verified with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` after the test repair; exit 0.
- **RF-008:** Verified with `git diff --check` after the test repair; exit 0.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts`, `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Explicit `sessions_spawn.model` forwards resolved provider/model to the child launch; in-process override authorization preserves scoped client metadata; no-explicit-model spawns do not become explicit provider/model overrides.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests assert the exact gateway `agent` request shape at the seam that starts the child run, avoiding live-provider flakiness while proving the routing data the gateway handler consumes.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** auth-provider, security-boundary, session-state, message-delivery, availability, compatibility, automation.
- **Risk explanation:** The change touches provider/model routing and gateway authorization for sub-agent launches. The public contract risk is limited to the existing `sessions_spawn.model` parameter; related open PRs were scanned by the daily-fix flow and treated as advisory background, not blockers. Message delivery/session fields are only moved in formatting around the same `agent` request object, not semantically changed.
- **Why acceptable:** Forwarding is gated on an explicit `sessions_spawn.model` value, so automatic/default model resolution is not converted into a gateway override. In-process authorization merges `allowModelOverride` into the scoped client instead of forcing a synthetic admin client, preserving plugin/run metadata. Regression tests cover explicit and no-explicit-model paths.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `spawnSubagentDirect` resolved `params.model` and persisted the resolved provider/model into the child session, but the subsequent gateway `agent` call that starts the child run did not include that resolved `provider`/`model`; the gateway handler can only honor explicit model routing from request fields it receives.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The patch changes the source-of-truth launch request before the child model is selected, rather than relying on status metadata or downstream fallback after the wrong route is chosen.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High: source-level regression tests cover the request shape, and local live gateway proof shows an explicit provider/model selected by the spawned child run. The only remaining proof gap is the reporter's exact QQ/Qwen/DeepSeek setup.
- **Patch quality notes:** Focused production diff plus regression tests. The timeout field appears in the patch only because the `agent` request object was wrapped to pass authorization options; the value and timeout behavior are unchanged. No guard/catch/default workaround or lockfile change.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** Owner boundary is `spawnSubagentDirect` constructing the child gateway `agent` request and `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcessRaw` selecting the gateway client metadata. This changes routing data before gateway model selection; it does not alter mirrored session status alone, public schema, or downstream provider fallback policy.

target.title: fix #95351: [Feature]: Generic JSONL line-parsing hook for CliBackendPlugin (native tool-card support beyond claude-stream-json)
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `CliBackendPlugin` backends that use `output: "jsonl"` had no public, backend-owned parser hook for provider-specific JSONL streams, so third-party CLIs with native tool execution could not feed OpenClaw's tool-card event path unless they impersonated a built-in dialect.
- Solution: Add an opt-in `parseJsonlEvent(line, ctx)` plugin hook that normalizes backend-native JSONL lines into existing assistant, thinking, result, session id, and display-only native tool events.
- What changed: The hook is exported through the plugin SDK, preserved through CLI backend resolution, passed into the CLI runner, and handled by `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` before built-in Claude/Gemini JSONL parsing. Plugin hook tool events use display-only tool-card callbacks so they do not mutate messaging delivery evidence.
- Follow-up update: Synced the branch onto current `origin/main` again as main moved, resolving `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` by regenerating the derived baseline and reconciling `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` with the current public SDK surface budget (`exports: 10413`, `callable exports: 5223`, `deprecated exports: 3257`). Current-head CI follow-up also regenerated `docs/docs_map.md` after `check-docs` found it stale. Earlier updates also removed the lint-only unnecessary test assertion flagged by ClawSweeper/CI.
- What did NOT change: This does not change the `agents.defaults.cliBackends.*.jsonlDialect` config schema, does not add a new built-in dialect value, does not execute plugin-reported tools through OpenClaw's tool catalog, does not let plugin display events count as message delivery evidence, and does not change Claude/Gemini stream-json semantics.
- Fixes #95351

## What Problem This Solves

Third-party `registerCliBackend` integrations can already launch JSONL-emitting CLIs, but OpenClaw's native tool-card path was tied to built-in Claude/Gemini stream dialects. A plugin with a different wire format had no canonical public contract for mapping already-executed backend tool calls to OpenClaw display events. This PR creates that contract while keeping provider-specific parsing owned by the backend plugin.

## Evidence

Local verification covered the parser behavior, backend resolution path, public SDK export surface, API baseline update, display-only runner isolation, lint cleanliness, strict build smoke, main-sync CI drift, and a local Control UI browser proof. The focused parser regression drives a Cursor-like JSONL sequence through `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` and observes assistant deltas, thinking commentary, native tool start/result deltas, final text, session id, and usage. The runner regression drives a plugin JSONL `message` tool card through `executePreparedCliRun` and verifies it renders tool events without setting messaging delivery evidence.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A plugin-owned CLI backend with `output: "jsonl"` can now translate provider-specific JSONL lines into OpenClaw display events, including native tool start/result cards, without selecting a built-in Claude or Gemini dialect.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on Windows/Git Bash with Node v22.17.0. The repository reports an engine warning for `>=22.19.0`, but the focused tests and build/lint checks below completed successfully in this environment.
- **Exact steps or commands run after the final update:**
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-output.test.ts src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts`
  - `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen`
  - `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`
  - `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts --reporter=verbose test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`
  - `pnpm docs:map:gen`
  - `pnpm docs:map:check`
  - `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:strict-smoke`
  - `git diff --check`
  - `pnpm lint --threads=8`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts --reporter=verbose src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts`
  - Earlier browser proof harness shaped as `node --import tsx <plugin-jsonl-ui-proof-harness>`
- **Evidence after fix:** `pnpm lint --threads=8` exited 0 after removing the unnecessary type assertion. target.title: fix(doctor): stop scaffolding empty safeBinProfiles that override built-in defaults
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw doctor --fix` silently weakened exec safe-bin security for anyone who added a built-in stdin-only helper (`cut`, `uniq`, `head`, `tail`, `tr`, `wc`, `grep`, `sort`, `jq`) to `tools.exec.safeBins`. Doctor scaffolded an empty `{}` profile for these bins, and because `resolveSafeBinProfiles` merges user profiles over the built-ins by key (not a deep merge), the empty `{}` wiped the built-in `maxPositional`, `allowedValueFlags`, and `deniedFlags`. The result was the worst of both worlds: the safe stdin-only form was rejected (e.g. `grep -e "pattern"`) while unsafe forms were allowed (e.g. `grep pattern file.txt`, `grep -r /`). The same empty-override hazard also lived in already-saved configs and was never repaired.

## Why This Change Was Made

doctor now distinguishes built-in bins from custom bins:

- Built-in bins are never scaffolded — their profile already applies at runtime. Plain `doctor` shows an informational note ("uses built-in profile (no custom override needed)") instead of a warning, and they are dropped from the `--fix` scaffold suggestion.
- Custom bins scaffold `{ maxPositional: 0 }` (a stdin-only default) instead of `{}`, matching the documented purpose of safeBins.
- The `safeBinProfiles` holder is created lazily, so doctor no longer leaves an empty `{}` object behind when nothing is scaffolded.
- An empty `{}` override of a built-in is flagged by plain `doctor` and **removed** by `doctor --fix` to restore the shipped profile. Detection is inheritance/fallback aware: it covers global scope, per-agent scope, agents that inherit the global `safeBins` list, and configs relying on the default safeBins set with no explicit `safeBins` key.

No config-shape, schema, or API change; no migration required (the runtime already reads the canonical shape — this only stops doctor from writing a harmful one and repairs existing harmful ones).

## User Impact

- Adding a built-in helper to `safeBins` keeps its built-in protections: the safe `-e`/stdin form works and unsafe file/recursive forms stay blocked.
- `doctor --fix` self-heals existing broken configs that contain an empty `{}` override of a built-in.
- Custom safeBins get a conservative stdin-only default scaffold instead of an unconstrained `{}`.

## Evidence

Tests (new + updated):

- `src/commands/doctor/shared/exec-safe-bins.test.ts`: built-in info note + no scaffold; custom `{ maxPositional: 0 }` scaffold; empty-override warn + `--fix` removal; explicit non-empty override preserved; global-`safeBins`-fallback (agent with no own safeBins) removal; default-safeBins (no `safeBins` key) detection; and a regression asserting `resolveSafeBinProfiles` returns the intact built-in `grep` profile after `--fix`.
- `src/commands/doctor/shared/preview-warnings.test.ts`: plain `doctor` warns about an empty built-in override even with no explicit `safeBins`.

Local validation (macOS):

- ~298 tests green across exec-safe-bins, preview-warnings, doctor-config-flow, repair-sequencing, security audit, exec-safe-bin policy/runtime, and agent-tools safe-bins.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `pnpm tsgo:core:test` clean for changed files (one unrelated pre-existing `packages/sdk/src/package.e2e.test.ts` error already on `main`).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on all changed files.

Review: the fix plan and the implementation were independently reviewed by Codex across three passes; all findings (inheritance/fallback detection gaps, message wording, and the plain-`doctor` preview gate for default-active safeBins) were addressed and confirmed resolved.

Notes: branched off latest `main`; independent of (and non-overlapping with) the other open PR on this fork.

target.title: fix #93908: [Bug]: [Bug]: Feishu plugin skipping discovery - host reports 2026.5.28 despite 2026.6.8 install
target.body:
Fixes #93908

## Summary

- Pin current-process post-core plugin update compatibility checks to the installed target OpenClaw version for both upgrades and downgrades.
- Pass the installed target version explicitly into mandatory post-core plugin convergence so it does not overwrite the target with the stale updater process `VERSION`.
- Sync this PR onto current `main` and preserve both the new ClawHub risk-acknowledgement plumbing and this PR's installed-target compatibility source of truth.
- Add regression coverage for the 2026.5.28 -> 2026.6.8 Feishu/plugin API compatibility path.

## What Problem This Solves

- Behavior or issue addressed: Feishu/Lark plugin discovery can be skipped after a package update when post-core plugin update logic still evaluates plugin API compatibility against the pre-update host version. The reported Feishu package declares `openclaw.compat.pluginApi: >=2026.6.8`, but a stale updater process can still report host `2026.5.28`, causing discovery to skip the plugin with `plugin requires plugin API >=2026.6.8, but this host is 2026.5.28; skipping discovery`.
- Why it matters / User impact: Users who update OpenClaw to a Feishu-compatible target can still lose Feishu channel availability because the post-core plugin phase rejects the installed plugin using stale current-process host state. That makes message delivery through Feishu unavailable even though the installed OpenClaw package is new enough.
- What did NOT change: This does not change Feishu package metadata, plugin API ranges, semver compatibility enforcement, plugin manifest parsing, default install choices, ClawHub trust/risk acknowledgement behavior, or runtime fallback behavior for genuinely incompatible plugins.
- Architecture / source-of-truth check: The public contract surface remains `openclaw.compat.pluginApi` and the existing compatibility resolver. The source of truth for post-core update compatibility is the installed target package version because that is the gateway version that will run after restart; this patch only feeds that target version into the existing resolver boundary.
- Related open PR scan: Related open PR #94019 improves compatibility diagnostic guidance, but it does not change discovery/version resolution/update handoff behavior. This PR targets the same-contract root cause in the update handoff rather than duplicating diagnostic text changes.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: The current-process post-core update path could still be running code whose module `VERSION` is the pre-update version (`2026.5.28`) while the installed package root had already been updated to `2026.6.8`. Fresh post-core child processes already receive `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION=<installed target>`, but the current-process path only pinned that override for downgrades. The convergence helper also overwrote inherited compatibility-host state with stale in-process `VERSION`.
- Why this is root-cause fix: Plugin compatibility during post-core update must be evaluated against the installed target package version, not the old updater process module state. Pinning `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION` to the installed target for the current-process plugin phase and passing the same target into convergence restores that lifecycle invariant, so the existing discovery gate makes the same decision the restarted gateway will make instead of masking the symptom with a Feishu-specific exception.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed target package version is the canonical source of truth for post-core plugin compatibility. This PR scopes the override to the post-core plugin phase and restores the caller's environment afterward, so normal runtime version resolution and explicit operator overrides outside the update handoff are unchanged.

When the installed target package version cannot be read, convergence keeps its previous fallback to the current runtime `VERSION`.

The latest update syncs onto current `main`; conflict resolution keeps main's ClawHub risk acknowledgement options flowing into post-core convergence while also keeping this PR's `compatibilityHostVersion` handoff.

## Verification

- Exact steps or commands run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts`; `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cli/update-cli.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts`; `pnpm tsgo:core`; `pnpm check:test-types`; `git diff --check`. All exited 0. Local `pnpm` printed the existing engine warning that the repo wants Node `>=22.19.0` while this machine has `v22.17.0`.
- Target test file: `src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts` covers the convergence helper using an explicit installed target over stale inherited host state; `src/cli/update-cli.test.ts` covers the current-process 2026.5.28 -> 2026.6.8 upgrade path pinning the environment during post-core plugin update and restoring it afterward.
- Scenario locked in: The regression tests lock in that a package update from host `2026.5.28` to installed target `2026.6.8` passes `2026.6.8` to plugin convergence and exposes `OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION=2026.6.8` while `updateNpmInstalledPlugins` runs, even though the updater process itself is still old.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The focused tests exercise the update/convergence lifecycle boundary that owns the stale-version handoff, while the Feishu discovery proof exercises the real plugin API decision. No broad end-to-end network fixture is needed to prove that discovery no longer uses the stale host version.

## Real behavior proof

- Real environment tested: Windows local worktree, current OpenClaw source, real Feishu package metadata from this repo (`@openclaw/feishu` version `2026.6.8`, `openclaw.compat.pluginApi: >=2026.6.8`).
- Evidence after fix: With stale update-process state (`OPENCLAW_VERSION=2026.5.28`) and compatibility host pinned to `2026.5.28`, Feishu was not discovered and discovery emitted `plugin requires plugin API >=2026.6.8, but this host is 2026.5.28; skipping discovery`. With the same stale `OPENCLAW_VERSION=2026.5.28` but compatibility host pinned to the installed target `2026.6.8`, Feishu was discovered and no plugin API skip diagnostic was emitted.
- Observed result after fix: The decision boundary from #93908 changes from “stale host rejects Feishu” to “installed target host discovers Feishu”; this confirms the post-core compatibility host version is the variable that controls the reported skip.
- What was not tested: A Feishu network/message round trip was not completed. A temporary Feishu app credential was available, but this local environment could not complete the external `open.feishu.cn` fetch; the submitted proof covers the Windows/local discovery and update-version behavior that caused the skip.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 (installed package version as compatibility source of truth):** Addressed by keeping the installed target package version as the explicit `compatibilityHostVersion` for post-core convergence and by preserving the environment override during current-process plugin update checks. This remains a compatibility source-of-truth choice for maintainers to accept, but the implementation and tests now consistently express that boundary.
- **RF-002 (live Feishu proof gap):** Disclosed. The available proof covers the Windows/local Feishu discovery and update-version decision boundary; it does not claim a live Feishu message round trip or full Windows npm-global update flow.
- **RF-003 (maintainer acceptance required):** Disclosed. The remaining non-code decision is maintainer acceptance of the installed target package version as the compatibility source of truth during post-core update; the latest code repair only resolves main-sync conflicts and keeps the PR mergeable.

## Regression Test Plan

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for the update/plugin convergence version handoff; it changes the source-of-truth handoff used by existing compatibility checks rather than adding a Feishu-specific exception.
- Patch quality notes: The only type escape touched here is the pre-existing test style for constructing a minimal `OpenClawConfig` fixture (`as unknown as OpenClawConfig`); production code does not add a type escape. Patch-quality warning handling is explicit: this is not a guard/default/catch fallback, and the code changes the lifecycle source of truth used by existing compatibility checks.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the stale-version handoff and discovery decision boundary because the production path has focused regression tests plus real Feishu metadata discovery proof. The lower-confidence area is external Feishu network delivery, which is disclosed as not tested.

## Merge risk

- Risk labels considered: `merge-risk:availability`, `merge-risk:compatibility`, `merge-risk:update`, `merge-risk:plugin-runtime`.
- Risk explanation: Post-core update compatibility checks affect installed external plugin update/discovery behavior and therefore plugin availability after update. The change is intentionally narrow: during the post-core plugin phase, use the installed target package version that will run after restart. It does not relax compatibility checks, does not change public config/schema/protocol, and does not introduce a new config/env surface.
- Why acceptable: The fresh child process already uses this installed-target-version contract. This PR makes the current-process path and convergence helper follow the same contract, restores the previous environment after the scoped phase, preserves main's ClawHub risk acknowledgement flow, and preserves the existing runtime `VERSION` fallback if the target version cannot be read.

## Non-goals

- Do not change Feishu package metadata or plugin API requirements.
- Do not relax or bypass plugin API compatibility checks.
- Do not add runtime fallbacks for incompatible plugins.

target.title: improve: ship 3D rendered lobster favicon for Control UI
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI uses a flat, hand-drawn 2D lobster as its favicon and logo. This PR upgrades that mascot to a 3D-rendered version of the **same lobster**, giving the browser tab icon, the login screen logo, and the installed PWA icon a more polished, modern look without changing the brand identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The four favicon assets in `ui/public/` are replaced in place, keeping the exact same filenames so no markup, manifest, or TypeScript changes are needed:

- `favicon.svg` — now a self-contained SVG that embeds the 3D bitmap as a base64 `data:` URI inside a single `<image>` element. Because the login page and agent logo already reference `favicon.svg`, they pick up the new art automatically.
- `favicon-32.png` — 32×32 raster of the 3D lobster.

target.title: fix(session): clear stale fallback model state on reset
target.body:
## Summary

Refs #90496.

This fixes the reset/session-target portion of the Discord oversized-session report:

- Clear stale runtime model, context-window, fallback notice, and harness metadata when `/new` or `/reset` rotates a reply session.
- Treat source-less model overrides as recovered auto-fallback state when persisted fallback-notice metadata shows the override is the fallback active model.
- Reuse that provenance in cron fresh-session sanitization so `session:<key>` jobs do not re-pin a reset channel to stale `codex/gpt-5.4` state.
- Preserve the existing compatibility rule for source-less legacy user-selected model overrides.

## Root Cause

`/new` and `/reset` created a new session id, but the session store merge could keep stale runtime fields such as `modelProvider`, `model`, `contextTokens`, and fallback notice metadata from the previous row. Source-less fallback model overrides were also treated as legacy user choices unless fallback origin metadata existed, so a stale fallback-active `codex/gpt-5.4` override could survive reset and cron fresh-session rollover.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: After `/new`/`/reset` or fresh cron session rollover, a source-less auto fallback override with fallback notice metadata no longer keeps a Discord channel/session-target lane pinned to stale `codex/gpt-5.4`; source-less legacy user-selected overrides are still preserved.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, using the repo Node/Vitest wrappers. No live Discord token, channel, or provider credential was used.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
pnpm format:check src/config/sessions/model-override-provenance.ts src/config/sessions/reset-preserved-selection.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/session.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/session.test.ts
git diff --check

.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --prompt 'Review the local fix for openclaw/openclaw#90496. The patch should clear stale source-less auto-fallback model state on /new/reset and fresh cron sessions without dropping legacy user-selected source-less model overrides.'
```

Evidence after fix:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...` passed 2 shards: cron session tests `16 passed`; auto-reply session tests `98 passed`.
- `pnpm format:check ...` reported all matched files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `pnpm changed:lanes --json` reports only core/coreTests paths for the six touched session/cron files.
- `autoreview` reported: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`.

Observed result after fix: The new regression tests show `/new`/`/reset` and fresh cron rollover clear stale fallback-active `codex/gpt-5.4` state, including persisted store fields, while preserving source-less legacy user-selected `codex/gpt-5.5` overrides.

What was not tested: No live Discord repro, no live Codex provider 4xx compaction call, no automatic transcript-preserving rotate policy change, and no full `pnpm check`/remote Testbox gate.

## Dependency Contract Checked

Codex upstream was checked directly. A failed compaction emits an error and does not install replacement history; replacement history is installed only after successful compaction. This PR therefore fixes OpenClaw's reset/session state cleanup path rather than changing Codex compaction semantics. Relevant files checked: `../codex/codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs`, `../codex/codex-rs/core/src/compact_remote.rs`, and `../codex/codex-rs/core/src/compact_remote_v2.rs`.

target.title: fix(feishu): tool calls use bound account outside inbound messages
target.body:
﻿Closes #96657

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu resource tools could run outside inbound Feishu messages without `ctx.agentAccountId`. In multi-account setups, that let wiki, drive, permission, bitable, doc, and app-scope tool calls fall back to global `channels.feishu.defaultAccount` instead of the Feishu account bound to the active session or agent.

That can route a tool call through the wrong Feishu app/tenant and surface as permission failures such as Feishu `99991672` or HTTP 403.

## Change

The resolver now keeps explicit/contextual accounts first, then checks Feishu bindings before the global default:

1. explicit tool `accountId`
2. valid `ctx.agentAccountId`
3. unique runtime Feishu account bound to `ctx.sessionKey`
4. unique configured Feishu `bindings[]` account for the current agent
5. first enabled account that supports the requested Feishu tool family
6. `channels.feishu.defaultAccount`

Ambiguous runtime or configured Feishu bindings fail closed instead of silently choosing `defaultAccount`.

This stays inside the Feishu extension and no longer adds a private routing SDK subpath.

## Evidence

Redacted live multi-account proof was run with default account `a` and bound account `b`: before the fix the same non-inbound Feishu resource call used `a` and failed; after the fix it used `b` and succeeded.

Focused tests cover runtime binding, configured binding, ambiguity, contextual account precedence, and capability fallback before default.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/tool-account-routing.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/docx.account-selection.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/tool-account.test.ts` - passed, 36 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/contracts/extension-package-project-boundaries.test.ts -- -t "xai|package boundary map"` - passed
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` - passed; public SDK remains 322 entrypoints / 10405 exports / 5223 callable exports
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check` - passed
- `git diff --check` - passed

Full extension package compile was started and passed Feishu, then stopped later on the pre-existing unrelated `qa-lab` `providerUrl/providerHeaders` type errors.

## Scope

This PR covers Feishu resource tools only. `feishu_chat` remains separate.

target.title: fix(followup): honor suppressToolErrors for queued tool progress
target.body:
Related: pattern sweep ledger 2026-07-01 suppressToolErrors followup sibling
Related PR: #97135

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where queued follow-up turns could still send failed tool-result progress to the originating channel when `messages.suppressToolErrors` was enabled.

The direct reply path already treats `messages.suppressToolErrors` as an explicit operator opt-out for visible tool-error progress. The queued follow-up runner used a separate tool-summary delivery path, so a queued follow-up could still route an `isError: true` tool payload even in a config that requested suppression.

## Why This Change Was Made

The follow-up runner now applies the same `messages.suppressToolErrors` guard at the shared queued tool-summary delivery seam used by embedded follow-ups and CLI tool summaries. Final failure handling and non-error tool progress are left unchanged.

This is narrower than #97135's recovered-progress policy: #97135 preserves full-verbose failed diagnostics when the operator has not opted out, while this PR makes the explicit `messages.suppressToolErrors` config win even in full verbose queued follow-ups.

Risk note: this touches a config-sensitive reply path, so the regression tests cover both the enabled suppression case and the normal unsuppressed full-verbose case, including final reply delivery in both cases.

## User Impact

Users who opt into `messages.suppressToolErrors` no longer see failed tool progress leak from queued follow-up replies. Users without that setting keep the existing full-verbose failed-tool progress behavior.

## Evidence

Head: `e9859a34b9b8`

Real queued follow-up runtime proof, no Vitest mocks:

- Command shape: `PROOF_SUPPRESS=<0|1> node --import tsx /tmp/tmp.hPhEcjgcTG.mjs`
- What it drives: the real exported `createFollowupRunner`, real `runEmbeddedAgent`, and a local OpenAI-compatible mock provider. The provider returns an `exec` tool call with `{ "command": "false" }`, then a final assistant message after receiving the tool output.
- Why this is scoped proof: it exercises the queued follow-up delivery seam before channel transport, records the routed `onBlockReply` payloads, and avoids real API spend.

﻿Closes #97032

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where edit tool `oldText` mismatch failures only showed the generic exact-match error plus current file contents, leaving users to guess whether indentation, escaping, or nearby text drift caused the miss.

## Why This Change Was Made

The edit mismatch path now appends bounded nearest-candidate diagnostics with line numbers, escaped line diffs, and indentation hints when the failing edit can be identified. Matching behavior is unchanged: the tool still requires the same exact/fuzzy edit semantics, and validation-phase no-op mismatch errors avoid candidate guesses when the indexed edit source is ambiguous.

## User Impact

Users and agents get actionable feedback after a failed edit call: the error can point at nearby candidate lines and show the visible difference, while still preserving the existing current-file-content hint.

## Evidence

- Real behavior proof: ran `node --import tsx` against `createEditTool()` on a temp file and intentionally submitted an `oldText` indentation mismatch. Result: the thrown edit-tool error included `Nearest candidate lines:`, `Candidate 1 (line 2):`, `indentation: expected 6 spaces, candidate 2 spaces`, and escaped diff lines (`- "      return value;"` / `+ "  return value;"`) after the redacted `Current file contents:` block.

target.title: fix(qqbot): strip echoed inbound metadata from replies
target.body:
﻿Closes #97980

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQ Bot users could see OpenClaw's internal inbound metadata at the start of replies, such as `Conversation info (untrusted metadata)` and `Sender (untrusted metadata)` JSON blocks, before the actual assistant response.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQ Bot now runs outbound-visible text through a plugin-owned sanitizer that keeps the existing assistant-visible text cleanup and strips leading echoed inbound metadata blocks before delivery. The same sanitizer is used by the QQ outbound adapter surface, by the direct QQ gateway dispatch path, and by the official C2C streaming path.

The direct QQ gateway path sanitizes block reply text before silent-reply classification as well as before delivery. That keeps metadata-prefixed `NO_REPLY` and `[SKIP]` control replies suppressed instead of stripping the metadata after the silence check and accidentally sending the control token.

The official C2C streaming path still keeps raw text for reply-boundary detection, but sanitizes the normalized visible text before starting or updating a QQ stream. Metadata-only partial updates are held until real visible answer text arrives, so the metadata block is not streamed first.

The change stays local to the QQ Bot plugin and does not alter the prompt envelope sent to the model.

## User Impact

QQ Bot replies no longer expose technical OpenClaw context blocks to end users when a model echoes the inbound prompt metadata. Users see only the intended assistant response text across adapter sends, direct static dispatch, and official C2C streaming, and metadata-prefixed silent replies remain silent.

## Evidence

Duplicate PR gate before implementation:

```text
gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --match title,body --limit 20 --json number,title,url,body,updatedAt -- "97980"
gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --match title,body --limit 20 --json number,title,url,body,updatedAt -- "内部元数据 渲染 用户聊天框"
gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --match title,body --limit 20 --json number,title,url,body,updatedAt -- "qqbot Conversation info Sender untrusted metadata"
```

Observed result: no open PRs matched #97980 or the QQ Bot metadata leak keywords.

Focused tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts
# passed: 2 files, 33 tests
```

The focused tests cover:

- QQ Bot outbound adapter sanitizer strips raw/fenced inbound metadata blocks.
- Direct gateway dispatch strips metadata from a normal block reply before QQ delivery.
- Direct gateway dispatch keeps metadata-prefixed `NO_REPLY` suppressed.
- Official C2C streaming does not send metadata-only partial chunks and streams only `final answer` once visible answer text arrives.

Formatting, diff hygiene, and local review:

```text
corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/visible-text.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/streaming-c2c.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts
# passed

git diff --check
# passed

.agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local
# passed with no reported output
```

Real sanitizer proof using the production QQ Bot visible-text helper with the issue's metadata shape:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module
# input: leading Conversation info + Sender JSON metadata blocks followed by "final answer"
# output: { "sanitized": "final answer" }
```

Follow-up after ClawSweeper review:

```text
# ClawSweeper reported that metadata-prefixed NO_REPLY/[SKIP] could be stripped after the silent check.
# Fixed by sanitizing block reply text before silent classification and delivery planning.
# Added regression coverage for metadata-prefixed NO_REPLY remaining suppressed.
# Also sanitized the official C2C streaming visible text path and added coverage that metadata-only partial replies are not streamed.
```


Live QQ Bot proof (2026-06-30, redacted):

```text
# isolated config/state used for proof only; QQBot AppID and user openid redacted
node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 19037 --force --verbose

[qqbot] WebSocket connected
[qqbot] Gateway ready
[qqbot] Dispatch event: t=C2C_MESSAGE_CREATE, d={"author":{"user_openid":"[REDACTED_OPENID]"},"content":"/bot-ping", ...}
[qqbot] Slash command matched: /bot-ping
[qqbot:api] >>> POST https://api.sgroup.qq.com/v2/users/[REDACTED_OPENID]/messages
[qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
```

Copied live QQ Desktop output from the same bot chat:

```text
user: /bot-ping
bot: ✅ pong!
     ⏱ 延迟：1820ms
     ├ 网络传输：1819ms
     └ 插件处理：1ms

# sent through real `openclaw message send --channel qqbot` to the same C2C target
# original outbound input intentionally started with:
#   Conversation info (untrusted metadata): {...}
#   Sender (untrusted metadata): {...}
bot: final answer from live QQBot proof
```

Observed result: the live QQ client showed only `final answer from live QQBot proof` for the metadata-shaped proof send. The `Conversation info (untrusted metadata)` and `Sender (untrusted metadata)` prefixes did not appear in the user-visible QQ Bot message. The CLI send returned a real QQBot platform message id for that delivery.
Live QQ Bot account conversation: tested with redacted QQBot credentials in an isolated local config/state directory. The live proof used a real QQ Bot WebSocket session, a real C2C inbound `/bot-ping`, and a real `openclaw message send --channel qqbot` delivery to the same C2C target.

Follow-up after ClawSweeper waiting-on-author review (commit f2f71b291c):

```text
# ClawSweeper asked for QQ Bot sanitizer coverage beyond Conversation info and Sender.
# Extended the plugin-owned sanitizer to strip the full known leading inbound metadata sentinel set:
# Thread starter, Reply target, Forwarded message context, and Chat history.
# Added focused adapter/direct dispatch/C2C streaming regression coverage for the expanded metadata chain.

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts
# passed: 2 files, 33 tests

pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/visible-text.ts
# passed
```

target.title: fix(ui): keep landscape composer compact
target.body:
Closes #98615

AI-assisted by Codex. Agent transcript logs were not included because transcript insertion needs explicit approval.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android Chrome PWA users in landscape orientation could have the Control UI composer occupy nearly the full screen, leaving too little chat history visible while composing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The short-landscape chat layout now bounds the composer height and keeps overflow inside the composer and textarea scroll areas, while reserving visible vertical space for the chat thread. The slash command menu is kept inside the bounded short-landscape composer as a sticky scrollable panel so the new composer scrollport does not clip the existing command UI.

## User Impact

Users on short landscape viewports, including Android PWA users, can keep the composer controls and slash command menu available while still seeing meaningful chat history above the input bar.

## Evidence

- Current head: `4c43ccf557b622744ac9b9dcce970daebb8dba0c`.
- Claim proved: the 568x320 short-landscape browser fixture keeps the composer bounded, leaves 40% of the viewport for the chat thread, keeps the textarea compact and scrollable, keeps attachment/toolbar rows scroll-reachable, and keeps the slash command menu visible inside the bounded composer without clipping.
- Added regression coverage: `ui/src/ui/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` now covers a short-landscape composer with an attachment row plus a long draft, verifies composer overflow, verifies model/settings/send controls after composer scroll, and verifies a slash menu remains visible and scrollable inside the bounded composer.
- Visual proof gist: https://gist.github.com/qingminglong/72855897728f4d1cc262494109c20a3c.
- Visual proof screenshots: slash menu visible at 568x320 (`short-landscape-slash-menu-top.svg` raw: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/qingminglong/72855897728f4d1cc262494109c20a3c/raw/4c076c87a04c7acb8487e017abae30da3ef5c2b8/short-landscape-slash-menu-top.svg) and controls reachable after composer scroll (`short-landscape-controls-scrolled.svg` raw: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/qingminglong/72855897728f4d1cc262494109c20a3c/raw/834d90aee0658f17335361c7f383c537ca9b0698/short-landscape-controls-scrolled.svg).
- Visual proof metrics JSON: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/qingminglong/72855897728f4d1cc262494109c20a3c/raw/a616148412674e77e635cad322add4ce76358636/short-landscape-slash-menu-metrics.json. Key metrics: viewport 568x320, composer 115.1875px, chat thread 128px, slash menu 88px with `scrollHeight` 138 > `clientHeight` 86, composer `scrollHeight` 313 > `clientHeight` 113, and after composer scroll the model/settings/send controls remain inside `.agent-chat__input`.
- `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH='C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe' node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts --reporter=verbose` - passed, 25 tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.ui.json --incremental false --pretty false` - passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint.CMD ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css ui/src/ui/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` - passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css ui/src/ui/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` - clean, no accepted/actionable findings reported.
- GitHub checks on current head: `Real behavior proof`, `preflight`, and `security-fast` passed; the broader CI matrix is still in progress.
- Not tested: physical Android Chrome PWA device capture; the closest available proof is the 568x320 Edge/Playwright short-landscape visual capture above.

target.title: fix(google-vertex-adc): bound token response body read to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` function in `vertex-adc.ts` buffers the full Google OAuth token response before parsing. A malicious or misconfigured OAuth endpoint could send a very large response, causing the gateway process to run out of memory.

This is the same class of issue as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98424 but in the Google Vertex token-refresh path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code used `response.arrayBuffer()` which buffers the entire response body in memory before parsing. This PR replaces that with `readResponseWithLimit` from the plugin SDK, which uses a streaming reader with a 16 MiB byte cap.

### Changes in this iteration (v3)

**Replaced ISIZE pre-check with bounded gunzip (`maxOutputLength`):**
- The previous ISIZE (gzip trailer uncompressed size) pre-check was modulo 2^32 and could be bypassed by a 4 GiB+ payload with ISIZE = 0
- Now uses Node.js zlib's `gunzipSync(bytes, { maxOutputLength })` which limits decompression output at the zlib layer before full allocation
- This is both more correct (zlib-native, not ad-hoc header parsing) and more secure (no modulo wrap-around)

**Fixed `content-encoding` header handling:**
- Removed the `content-encoding` header fallback from `shouldGunzipGoogleOauthTokenResponse`
- Node.js fetch auto-decompresses gzip bodies and may leave `content-encoding: gzip` on the response, causing `gunzipSync` to fail on already-decompressed data
- Now only checks gzip magic bytes (`0x1f 0x8b`) to decide whether to decompress

### Changes in this iteration (v4)

**Node 24 compatibility - gzip overflow error code:**
- Node 24.18.0's `gunzipSync` throws `ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE` (RangeError) when `maxOutputLength` is exceeded, not `ERR_ZLIB_OUTPUT_LENGTH_EXCEEDED` as on Node <24
- Updated the catch block to handle both error codes, ensuring correct behavior across all supported Node versions

**Removed proof script & added focused regression tests:**
- Deleted `scripts/proof-real-behavior.mjs` (the inlined proof script)
- Restored `extensions/google/vertex-adc.test.ts` with 11 focused tests covering all bounded-read and overflow scenarios

## User Impact

None under normal operation. ADC token responses are typically < 10 KiB. The 16 MiB cap is far above any legitimate response size.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — production module via HTTP (Node 24.18.0)

Imports `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` from the **actual built production module** (`dist/extensions/google/vertex-adc.js`) and exercises it against a local HTTP server with real `fetch()` requests — no inline implementation, no mocking.

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  Real Behavior Proof — PR #98507
║  Production module: dist/extensions/google/vertex-adc.js
║  Node: v24.18.0
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

  ✅ Normal token response
  ✅ Gzip-compressed token (raw bytes, no content-encoding header)
  ✅ Oversized wire (~20 MB > 16 MiB)
  ✅ Gzip compressed overflow (raw bytes, 32 MiB → 32 KB wire)
  ✅ Empty body
  ✅ Invalid JSON
  ✅ OAuth error response

  Results: 7 passed, 0 failed
  Production module: dist/extensions/google/vertex-adc.js
```

### Unit tests (focus on bounded read behavior)

11 dedicated regression tests in `extensions/google/vertex-adc.test.ts`:

```
 ✓ parses a valid token response
 ✓ returns undefined for an empty body
 ✓ returns undefined for invalid JSON
 ✓ handles gzip-compressed token responses
 ✓ parses error responses with error_description
 ✓ throws on response exceeding 16 MiB via stream
 ✓ succeeds on response just under 16 MiB via stream
 ✓ handles non-streaming Response via arrayBuffer fallback
 ✓ throws on non-streaming oversized response via arrayBuffer fallback
 ✓ throws on gzip response that decompresses past decoded cap
 ✓ handles whitespace-only body gracefully
```

### Key findings

1. Normal token responses — bounded reader accepts without regression
2. Gzip-compressed token responses — decompressed and parsed correctly (magic-byte detection, no content-encoding dependency)
3. Oversized wire responses (>16 MiB) — caught with descriptive error; memory bounded
4. Gzip compressed overflow (small wire, huge decompressed) — caught by the bounded gunzip `maxOutputLength` option on both Node <24 (`ERR_ZLIB_OUTPUT_LENGTH_EXCEEDED`) and Node 24+ (`ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE`)
5. Empty body and invalid JSON — handled gracefully (returns undefined)
6. OAuth error responses — `error_description` parsed correctly
7. The 16 MiB cap is far above expected ADC token responses (< 10 KiB)

target.title: fix(nostr): clear per-relay publish timeout timer to prevent dangling handles
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #98463

`publishProfileEvent` in `extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile.ts` creates a `setTimeout` per relay to enforce `RELAY_PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_MS`, but the returned timer handle was discarded. When a relay accepted the event quickly (the common success path), the timeout callback had already been scheduled and would remain active until it fired 5 seconds later. On busy agents that publish profiles repeatedly, these dangling timers accumulate and increase memory/FD pressure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix saves the `setTimeout` handle and clears it in a `finally` block, so the timer is cancelled whether the publish succeeds, times out, or throws. This matches the timer lifecycle already used in sibling Nostr modules (`nostr-bus.ts` and `nostr-profile-import.ts`).

## User Impact

- Nostr profile publishing no longer leaks per-relay timer handles.
- Long-running agents with frequent profile updates see reduced stale timer accumulation.
- No behavioral change for callers: successes/failures/timeouts are still reported the same way.

## Evidence

Unit tests in `extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile.test.ts`:

```
✓ clears the per-relay timeout timer after a successful publish
✓ clears the per-relay timeout timer after a publish timeout
✓ does not add dangling timers when publishing to multiple relays
```

Run:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile.test.ts --run
```

Result: 34 passed.

Lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile.ts extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile.test.ts` → exit 0.
Typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` → exit 0.
Build: `pnpm build` → exit 0.

## Real behavior proof

I wrote a standalone Node.js script that monkey-patches `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` to count active "publish timeout" timers after the real exported `publishProfile()` function returns. The script runs against real Node timers (no Vitest fake timers).

**BEFORE (source fix reverted):**

```
--- success path (promise resolves fast) ---
relays: 2
successes: 2
failures: 0
active timers before call: 0
active timers after call: 2
dangling timer age: 2ms
dangling timer age: 1ms

--- timeout path (promise never resolves) ---
relays: 2
successes: 0
failures: 2
active timers before call: 0
active timers after call: 0

=== Summary ===
success path dangling timers: 2
timeout path dangling timers: 0
FAIL: dangling timers detected after publishProfile() returned
```

The leak appears only on the success path: when `pool.publish` resolves before the 5 s timeout, the old code never cleared the timer.

**AFTER (this patch):**

```
--- success path (promise resolves fast) ---
relays: 2
successes: 2
failures: 0
active timers before call: 0
active timers after call: 0

--- timeout path (promise never resolves) ---
relays: 2
successes: 0
failures: 2
active timers before call: 0
active timers after call: 0

=== Summary ===
success path dangling timers: 0
timeout path dangling timers: 0
PASS: no dangling timers detected after publishProfile() returned
```

**Negative control:** reverting only the source change while keeping the new tests makes the success-path test fail to observe a clean timer state, confirming the tests are sensitive to the fix.

- **Behavior addressed:** per-relay `setTimeout` handle created during `publishProfile` is now cleared after the race finishes.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node v22.19+, local source checkout.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile.test.ts --run`.
- **Evidence after fix:** all 34 tests pass; standalone timer probe shows 0 dangling timers in both success and timeout paths.
- **Observed result after fix:** no active `RELAY_PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_MS` timers remain after `publishProfile` returns.
- **What was not tested:** live relay WebSocket behavior; the fix only touches local timer lifecycle and does not change relay protocol handling.

## Related issues

- #98463

target.title: fix(webchat): slash menu clipped by overflow and missing keyboard scroll
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: The webchat slash command menu (`/`) is completely invisible — typing `/` changes the input border color and arrow-key selection works, but the dropdown never appears. This is because `.agent-chat__input` uses `overflow: hidden` (for textarea scroll containment), which clips the absolutely-positioned slash menu that renders above the input via `position: absolute; bottom: 100%`.
- Additionally, when the slash menu has more items than the visible scroll area, keyboard navigation (ArrowUp/ArrowDown) does not auto-scroll the active item into view — users must manually scroll with the mouse.
- What changed: Introduced `.agent-chat__input-wrap` as a positioning parent for the slash menu, so it renders outside the `overflow: hidden` container. Added `scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" })` after each arrow-key index change.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): No modifications to slash command logic, command execution, or any non-UI code.

![slash-menu-fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9623f14a-9a7d-43a8-82fe-f75d5be85ba2)
- Here above demonstrates the fix.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Slash command menu now appears above the input box when typing `/` in webchat.
- Arrow-key navigation in the slash menu auto-scrolls to keep the active item visible.
- No changes to existing keyboard shortcuts (Tab to fill, Enter to select, Escape to close).

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.2.0)
- Runtime/container: Node.js 22+
- Integration/channel: Webchat (Control UI)

### Steps

1. Start gateway: `openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port 18789 --force`
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:18789/webchat/`
3. Type `/` in the chat input

### Expected

- Slash command menu appears above the input box
- ArrowDown/ArrowUp navigates through commands with auto-scroll

### Actual (before fix)

- Input border changes color (`:focus-within` fires), arrow keys + Enter work (DOM exists), but the menu is completely invisible — clipped by `overflow: hidden`
- When menu is made visible via other means, keyboard navigation past visible items requires manual mouse scrolling

## Evidence

- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Screenshot/recording

Before fix — typing `/` shows no menu (only border color change):
The DOM is present and functional (keyboard selection works), but the popup is clipped to zero height by `overflow: hidden` on the parent.

After fix — slash menu visible and keyboard-scrollable:
Menu appears above input; ArrowDown past visible items auto-scrolls the list.

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios:
  - Built UI locally via `pnpm ui:build`, started gateway with `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`
  - Confirmed slash menu appears when typing `/`
  - Confirmed ArrowDown/ArrowUp auto-scrolls active item into view
  - Confirmed Tab fills command, Enter selects, Escape closes
  - Confirmed input box border-radius, textarea scroll, and backdrop-filter unaffected
  - Confirmed mobile layout selector updated (`.agent-chat__input-wrap` in `layout.mobile.css`)
- What I did **not** verify:
  - macOS/iOS native app webchat (only tested browser webchat)

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert the `.agent-chat__input-wrap` wrapper — move `margin`/`flex-shrink` back to `.agent-chat__input` and remove the wrapper `<div>` in `chat.ts`.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: If a CSS rule targets `.agent-chat__input` for margin/positioning, it may need updating to `.agent-chat__input-wrap`.

## Files changed

- `ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css` — Added `.agent-chat__input-wrap` class; moved `margin` and `flex-shrink` from `.agent-chat__input` to the wrapper
- `ui/src/styles/layout.mobile.css` — Updated mobile override selector from `.agent-chat__input` to `.agent-chat__input-wrap`
- `ui/src/ui/views/chat.ts` — Wrapped input bar in `.agent-chat__input-wrap`; moved `renderSlashMenu` outside `.agent-chat__input`; added `scrollSlashMenuActiveIntoView()` helper called after ArrowUp/ArrowDown navigation

**AI-assisted:** Built with Claude Code. Tested manually on local gateway webchat.

target.title: fix(memory): pass request.proxy to embedding HTTP client for explicit…
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who configure `request.proxy` with `mode: "explicit-proxy"` on a provider (e.g. Cohere) would find that memory search embedding requests ignore the proxy and fail with connection errors, while chat/completions requests from the same provider successfully route through the proxy.

This affects users in restricted network environments where the embedding API endpoint is unreachable directly but accessible through a configured proxy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedding HTTP call chain read `baseUrl`, `apiKey`, and `headers` from the provider config but did not read `request.proxy`. The chat/completions path already supports `request.proxy` via `dispatcherPolicy`.

This change plumbs `providerConfig.request.proxy` through the embedding call chain as a `dispatcherPolicy` parameter, matching the existing pattern used by chat/completions.

## User Impact

Users can now configure `request.proxy` on a provider and have both chat/completions AND memory search embedding requests route through the proxy. No configuration changes needed.

Backward-compatible: no behavior change when `request.proxy` is not configured.

## Evidence

Tested on a deployment in China where `api.cohere.ai` is blocked:
- Before: `memory_search` failed with 403 from Cohere embedding endpoint
- After: `memory_search` succeeds (5.3s) with embedding requests routed through proxy

target.title: fix(gateway): show pending node approval diagnostics
target.body:
﻿Closes #98045

AI-assisted by Codex. Agent transcript logs were not included because transcript insertion needs explicit approval.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users diagnosing Android/node reconnect approval could see that approval was pending but still not discover the exact node approval request id or the `openclaw nodes approve <requestId>` command from Gateway diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused Gateway diagnostics command, `openclaw gateway diagnostics node-approvals`, that uses the existing pairing-aware node diagnostics path and renders only pending node approval/reapproval entries with the exact approve command. It preserves safe connection guidance for explicit `--url`, `--token`, and `--password` use without printing credential values, and threads password auth through the node CLI RPC path so the follow-up `nodes approve` command can reuse the same auth mode.

## User Impact

Operators can now run a Gateway diagnostics command and copy the exact node approval command instead of guessing `openclaw devices approve <ip>` or hunting through node status output.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: the new diagnostics command renders pending node approval IDs and exact approve commands, requests the pairing-aware node diagnostics path needed for pending request IDs, and preserves non-leaking connection/auth guidance for explicit remote credentials.
- Patch blocker fixed at head `1a21756ad2`: `renderPendingNodeApprovalDiagnostic` now returns before formatting/sanitizing when `pendingRequestId` is absent, so `requestId` is narrowed to `string` before `sanitizeForLog(requestId)`.

target.title: feat: add operator audit history for agent runs and tools
target.body:
Closes #98521

## What Problem This Solves

Operators currently have to correlate transient runtime output, session transcripts, and task records to answer who ran an agent or tool, what action occurred, when it happened, and how it ended. There is no single durable, bounded, redaction-safe query surface for those operational questions.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a typed metadata-only audit contract over the existing agent-run and tool lifecycle signals. Events use stable identities and database order, carry agent/session/actor provenance and closed result/error codes, and persist through one Kysely-backed table in the shared state database. The implementation reuses current lifecycle and transcript ownership rather than creating another conversation store.

The operator surfaces are the read-authorized `audit.list` Gateway method and `openclaw audit`, including bounded filters, cursor pagination, and bounded JSON output. Prompts, message bodies, tool arguments, tool results, and raw error text are excluded by contract.

## User Impact

Authorized operators can inspect recent agent-run and tool-action history by agent, session, actor, action, status, and time range. Records survive process restarts, retain deterministic ordering, and are capped by a 30-day retention window, a 100,000-row limit, and 500-row query pages.

## Evidence

- Focused local behavior proof (324 tests):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/audit/audit-event-writer.test.ts src/commands/audit.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts src/infra/agent-events.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts src/agents/command/attempt-execution.error-propagation.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts`
- Post-review regression proof:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/command/attempt-execution.error-propagation.test.ts src/commands/agent.acp.test.ts src/commands/agent.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/audit/audit-event-writer.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts src/agents/command/attempt-execution.error-propagation.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/control-plane/manager.turn-results.test.ts src/agents/command/attempt-execution.error-propagation.test.ts src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts`
- Generated surfaces verified clean:
  - `node --import tsx scripts/protocol-gen.ts`
  - `node --import tsx scripts/protocol-gen-swift.ts`
  - `node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mjs`
  - `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`
- Documentation checks:
  - `node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check`
  - `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md`
  - `node scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mjs`
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwf5ws6pfwj2tcsavsnc54hn`: full `check:changed` lane passed, including all-project typecheck, core/extension/script lint, database-first guard, and runtime import cycles ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28530060815)). The wrapper stopped the successful one-shot session, so the backing lifecycle job may display as cancelled after the command completed with exit 0.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwf7yk3968m7vh2634qabet9`: a real Gateway agent turn invoked one `exec` tool action, then `openclaw audit --json` returned four ordered metadata-only records ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28532183950)). The same run seeded the shared database from the pre-feature schema, preserved an existing row, added `audit_events` on open, proved a one-record page has a next cursor, and verified prompt/reply/tool-result sentinels plus unexpected fields were absent. Command and wrapper both exited 0; provider-owned one-shot cleanup may display the backing lifecycle job as cancelled.

  ```json
  {
    "gatewayHealth": "ok",
    "upgrade": { "existingStatePreserved": true, "auditTableAdded": true, "auditRows": 4 },
    "page": { "limit": 1, "eventCount": 1, "hasNextCursor": true },
    "redaction": { "contract": "metadata_only", "contentSentinelsAbsent": true, "unexpectedFieldsAbsent": true },
    "events": [
      { "sequence": 4, "kind": "agent_run", "action": "agent.run.finished", "status": "succeeded" },
      { "sequence": 3, "kind": "tool_action", "action": "tool.action.finished", "status": "succeeded", "toolName": "exec" },
      { "sequence": 2, "kind": "tool_action", "action": "tool.action.started", "status": "started", "toolName": "exec" },
      { "sequence": 1, "kind": "agent_run", "action": "agent.run.started", "status": "started" }
    ]
  }
  ```

- Fresh `koffing-updated` xhigh review against `origin/main`: clean, no accepted or actionable findings.
- Exact head `320e277fc6b354eae689496fbdd265a18b784380`: no pending or failing checks after the initial workflow run; scope and draft admission skipped the remaining checks, and GitHub reports no required checks configured.

## Risks and Non-Goals

- No Control UI is included; this PR provides the protocol and operator read foundation only.
- No new broad configuration surface is added. Retention and queue bounds are fixed safety limits for this foundation.
- No prompt, content, argument, result, or raw-error capture is added, and existing transcript files remain the only conversation artifacts.
- Draft PR #98510 overlaps only the generated `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift` protocol output. There is no runtime dependency, but whichever branch merges second will need to regenerate that additive shared file.

## AI Disclosure

AI-assisted implementation and review. Maintainer review remains required; no agent transcript is attached.
